repurposeSummary: Original 'Rainformer GPU #2 (HWiNFO Edition)' skin (Name in [Metadata] still reads that). All GPU-telemetry measures that normally read HWiNFO shared-memory sensors for GPU temperature/usage/memory/fan/clocks have been left in place, but the four measures that actually feed the visible meters were repointed to the MSIAfterburner.dll plugin's Framerate/Frametime DataSources. Gpu2Name variable was changed to 'FPS Counter' (rendered as 'FPS COUNTER' by the title's UPPER case style). Net effect: the panel now behaves as a generic frame-rate/frame-time HUD, but still carries dead GPU-specific code paths (memory %, fan RPM, per-GPU HWiNFO sensor IDs) that are computed but never displayed.

localVariables.note: Only these keys are set locally inside GPU2.ini's own [Variables] section; everything else is inherited from the three @Include files.

backgroundGeometry.note: All shape coordinates below are as authored (unscaled); Rainmeter then multiplies every coordinate by #Scale# (1.7) INSIDE the style's own formulas (baked-in scaling), rather than via a per-meter TransformationMatrix (StyleBackground itself carries no TransformationMatrix option).
backgroundGeometry.totalHeightFormula: [MeterBackgroundHeight:Y]*#Scale# - dynamic, depends on cumulative content height (see verticalFlowSummary / notes: not a fixed constant, grows/shrinks with which rows/graph are visible)

Shape4 (body, rounded bottom corners, dynamic height)

unscaledRect.h: [[#CURRENTSECTION]:H] - ((BgShapeX+12.3)*2)*Scale  (i.e. total panel height minus header block, computed dynamically)

shapes.name: Shape5 (union'd into body to square off its top edge)
Shape7 (outer frame, drawn over everything)

backgroundGeometry.twoZoneSummary: Header band ~ y=5..27 unscaled (rounded top corners only, fill BgTopColor light blue-violet 163,178,230@180) directly above a body band starting ~y=29 (square top / rounded bottom corners, fill BgBodyColor light grey 230,230,230@180). This is the shared two-zone rounded-rect background used across the whole Rainformer suite; only its total height is panel-specific (grows with number of visible rows + graph).

measures.name: GpuTemp
notes: Repurposed measure: despite its name, DataSource is Framerate, not a temperature sensor.
MinValue=1 (not 0) is a leftover from the original temperature semantics; harmless for the Line graph autoscale=0 clamp but worth preserving verbatim.

measures.name: GpuTempWarn
notes: IMPORTANT: thresholds are HARDCODED at 30/60/90/120 in this Formula, NOT the GpuTempWarnTh1-4 variables (45/55/65/75) that exist in Variables.inc. Those variables are unused dead config for this measure.

Because GpuTemp's value is now the live Framerate (not a temperature), the big FPS number's font color is driven by these leftover temp thresholds: FPS<30 -> DevTempWarnColorTh1 (47,186,255 sky blue); 30<=FPS<60 -> Th2 (255,255,36 yellow); 60<=FPS<90 -> Th3 (255,143,30 orange); 90<=FPS<120 -> Th4 (255,0,0 red); FPS>=120 -> Th5 (204,0,0 dark red).
Example from context screenshot: 51 FPS falls in the 30<=x<60 bracket -> font color should be yellow (255,255,36), NOT black/colorText as the base style would otherwise imply.

measures.name: GpuCoreUsage
notes: Same DataSource (Framerate) as GpuTemp - i.e. the same live FPS value is read into two independent measures and consequently plotted twice (red GpuTempHistogram line and light-blue GpuUsageHistogram line are literally identical data).

measures.name: GpuCoreUsageBarWarn
notes: Threshold (75) is compared against the RAW Framerate value (0-144 scale), not against the derived percent-of-144. So the bar turns crimson (220,20,60) whenever raw FPS > 75, otherwise stays GpuUsageColor (176,196,222).

measures.name: GpuCoreUsageScaled
notes: This is the hardcoded '/144*100 percent-of-refresh' formula referenced in the task brief: it expresses live Framerate as a percentage of a fixed 144 Hz reference, i.e. 'Framerate: 35%' for ~50.4 FPS.
144 is a literal constant in the .ini, not a variable - capture it verbatim.

usedBy: GpuMemUsageHistogram (line graph, colored with GpuMemUsageColor despite being 1% Low data)
notes: Repurposed: DataSource='Framerate 1% Low' (MSI Afterburner's 1% low framerate statistic).

measures.name: GpuMemoryClock
usedBy: GpuFanHistogram (line graph, colored with GpuFanColor despite being Frametime data)
notes: Repurposed: DataSource='Frametime' (milliseconds).

MaxValue=50 is a HARD CAP for the Line graph's autoscale=0 vertical scale: any Frametime value above 50ms is clamped/clipped to the top of the 25px-tall graph box. The context screenshot's example value (618.4ms, i.e. ~1.6 FPS) would render fully pinned at the graph's ceiling, not proportionally - important for pixel-perfect graph reproduction.

verticalFlowSummary: Header title 'FPS COUNTER' (Y=9, centered) -> big FPS number '%1FPS' colored by leftover temp-warn thresholds (Y=30, centered) -> row 'Framerate:' left / '<pct>%' right (Y=32) -> thin 1px usage bar directly beneath that row (Y=row-bottom+0) -> row '1p LOW: <val>FPS' (with opaque near-white backing plate) left / 'FRAMETIME: <val>ms' right (Y=bar-bottom+2) -> empty graph backdrop + up to 4 overlaid colored Line sparklines (red=Framerate dup #1, light-blue=Framerate dup #2, green=1% Low, cyan=Frametime) in one 188x25 box (Y=text-row-bottom+4) -> invisible alignment spacer (same box) -> invisible height-marker meter (+10) that drives the background shape's total height. Two text rows (Framerate/%, and 1p LOW/FRAMETIME) have Rainmeter-auto-sized (not fixed) heights, so exact final pixel Y of the bar/graph cannot be stated as a hardcoded constant purely from the .ini - a Direct2D reimplementation must measure its own DirectWrite text-layout height for 8pt Trebuchet MS (matching AccurateText=1 behavior) and apply the same RowSpacing(=1)/R-offset arithmetic documented per meter above.
notes: This is fundamentally still the stock Rainformer 'GPU #2 (HWiNFO Edition)' skin file (see [Metadata] Name) with its Variables/Styles pulled from the suite-wide @Resources includes; only Gpu2Name and the four MSIAfterburner DataSource overrides make it behave as an FPS panel. Anything not wired to a visible meter (GPU memory %, fan RPM/percent, per-GPU HWiNFO sensor ids, AMD/NVIDIA memory branching) is inert leftover code, still computed each cycle but never drawn.

Literal ini Text= strings have NO space between the numeric substitution and the unit suffix: '"%1FPS"', '1p LOW: %1FPS', 'FRAMETIME: %1ms'. Verified via direct UTF-16LE byte decode (not just visual transcription) - e.g. resolves to '51FPS', '1p LOW: 2FPS', 'FRAMETIME: 618.4ms'. This differs from the spacing shown in the task's example screenshot text ('51 FPS', '1p LOW: 2 FPS', 'FRAMETIME: 618.4 ms'); it's unclear whether that's a paraphrase in the brief or the MSIAfterburner plugin appends a leading space to its returned numeric string at runtime (plugins normally do not). Recommend reproducing the literal no-space ini text unless the live app is confirmed otherwise.

The big FPS number's font color is NOT a fixed color - it is bound to a Calc measure (GpuTempWarn) that recolors it based on the numeric FPS value crossing hardcoded thresholds 30/60/90/120, mapping to DevTempWarnColorTh1-5 (sky-blue/yellow/orange/red/dark-red). This is a direct side-effect of repurposing a temperature measure as a framerate measure and must be reproduced for pixel-perfect fidelity.

GpuCoreUsageBarWarn's '>75' crimson-highlight threshold on the usage bar compares against the RAW Framerate (0-144), not the displayed percent - i.e. bar+text turn crimson only when raw FPS exceeds 75, which is also >75/144=52% on the percent scale (same crossing point, just expressed on the raw axis).

GpuMemoryClock (Frametime) measure has MaxValue=50, hard-capping the frametime sparkline's vertical scale at 50ms; very low framerates (high frametimes, e.g. the screenshot's 618.4ms example) will render pinned flat at the top of the graph, not proportionally.

All four Graph enable-flags (GpuTempGraph/GpuUsageGraph/GpuMemUsageGraph/GpuFanGraph) plus GpuTemp/GpuUsage/GpuMem/GpuFan/GpuCoreMemClock/ShowGraph default to 1 in @Resources/Variables.inc, and GPU2.ini does not locally override any of them. Taken completely literally, ALL FOUR Line-graph meters (GpuTempHistogram/GpuUsageHistogram/GpuMemUsageHistogram/GpuFanHistogram) would be simultaneously visible, stacked exactly on top of each other in the same 188x25 box (all use Y=r chained off meterHistogram). The task's reference screenshot only describes a single frametime sparkline, so the live/actual Rainmeter instance this was captured from most likely has per-skin persisted overrides (written via the skin's right-click Settings UI / Settings.lua, which calls !WriteKeyValue against this same ini's [Variables] section) that were not present in the copy of GPU2.ini provided for extraction. Could not locate any such persisted override file in the provided folder tree. Recommend either (a) treating the frametime-only cyan line as the intended visual and disabling the other three in the reimplementation, or (b) confirming the live skin's on-disk [Variables] section for the true current flag values before finalizing.

colorHistogram/colorHistogramAlpha (176,196,222/250) is StyleGraph's default LineColor/PrimaryColor, but every one of the four Line meters overrides LineColor explicitly (GpuTempColor/GpuUsageColor/GpuMemUsageColor/GpuFanColor), and 'PrimaryColor' is not a documented option for Meter=Line (it applies to other meter types) - so colorHistogram itself never actually appears on screen in this panel; it's effectively dead/inherited-but-overridden.

MSIAfterburner.dll Plugin measures in this file specify no GPU-index/selector option - they read whichever single/aggregate frame-timing data MSI Afterburner's shared memory exposes by default, not something specific to a 'second GPU' despite the panel's GPU2 heritage.

TransformationMatrix='#Scale#;0;0;#Scale#;#Scale#;#Scale#' (Scale=1.7) is applied per-meter to every text/bar/line/image meter EXCEPT the background Shape meter (which bakes *#Scale# into its own coordinate formulas instead). All X/Y/W/H numbers captured above are the UNSCALED authored values as requested; multiply by 1.7 (and account for the matrix's translation term, which nudges the scaled result by an additional +Scale=+1.7px in both axes) to get final on-screen pixels.

AccurateText=1 (set at [Rainmeter] section level) means Rainmeter measures STRING meter bounding boxes via precise DirectWrite metrics rather than approximate GDI+ metrics - directly relevant since several row heights in this panel are auto-sized from text metrics rather than fixed H values.
